design.name: Hedgehog: game-day promos for any Austin bar, hedged on Gemini, guaranteed onchain
design.one_liner: "Your drink's on us if the Spurs lose": hedged on Gemini, guaranteed onchain. Kalshi signs up bars one at a time over the phone. With Hedgehog, any Austin bar, coffee cart or food truck types one sentence and gets a promo it can sell in 30 seconds. The promo is priced from Gemini's live book and hedged with real Gemini contracts before the first sale. The customers' refunds sit in a Solana escrow and land as dollars the customer owns.
design.lenses_applied:
This round I kept the 8.10 core: the one-merchant weather pair that is certain to pay, the hedge-gated Unhedged program rule, real production Gemini fills, crypto that stays invisible, and the attack panel. Then I fixed every objection that all four critics raised. I also avoided the two changes that got earlier versions rejected: a favorite ("Spurs WIN") as the hero promo, and store credit that cycles back to the merchant or mainnet on the critical path.

1) IDENTITY AND RIVALRY (jaded #1, #6). The one-liner is now one sentence. The problem slide shows four headlines (The Jeffrey $5K/Knicks, Rizzo's $2K/Mexico, TallBoy DC, The Blue Light SF "~40% more business"), all hedged by hand through Kalshi's /hedging outreach. That turns the copycat worry into proof of demand. The pitch says it outright: "Kalshi does this by phone for one bar at a time. Hedgehog is the self-serve, escrowed version, on Gemini." Gemini judges hear a competitive answer to Kalshi.

2) THE REFUND IS USEFUL AND STAYS THE CUSTOMER'S (all four critics; avoids the rejected 'store credit to merchant'). The refund is pushed as USDC into the customer's browser wallet. The customer owns it, and neither the merchant nor Hedgehog can claw it back. The receipt page then offers two buttons. 'Spend it here' turns the $1 into $1.25 off the next visit: the customer signs a transfer to the merchant, the merchant pays the fee, and the merchant adds a 25% bonus as the repeat-visit hook. This is Rizzo's 'gift card redeemable next visit' made programmable, and it is optional. 'Cash out' sends to any Solana or exchange deposit address. The escrow stays meaningful because money only flows back to the merchant when the customer chooses to spend it there. Labels are honest: in the hackathon the receipt says 'test dollars (devnet USDC); real USDC in production'.

3) HEDGE HELD, NOT JUST BOUGHT (sponsor #2). The attestor re-reads positions at sales cutoff and again 30 minutes before settlement. attest_hedge takes a phase argument (OPEN, CUTOFF or PRESETTLE), and the program stores hedge_held_bps for each phase. The receipt shows 'Hedge held at kickoff ✓'. A fifth stage attack sells 1 contract back on Gemini after cutoff. The receipt flips to 'Hedge reduced: your $1 is still in the vault'. This shows the split plainly: the vault guarantees the customer, the hedge guarantees the merchant.

4) TRUST STATED HONESTLY (jaded #4, past-winners #4, demo #7). Everywhere it is 'a program rule fed by a disclosed attestor', never 'trustless'. In the demo the attestor and relayer keys belong to one operator (Hedgehog). Key separation is presented as least privilege, not as more trust. The visible proof is the customer-side 'Verify with Gemini'.

5) CANONICAL RESOLUTION HASH (sponsor #5, demo #2). The stored hash covers only: ticker, each contract's instrumentSymbol and resolutionSide, and resolvedAt, serialized in sorted-key JSON. Volume fields are excluded. Verify is tested against an event resolved more than 24 h earlier before we record the video.

6) CALENDAR CORRECTED (demo #4, past-winners #1). The video uses only Thursday settlements: the Spurs promo, about 10 PM CT Thu, and the Thursday weather pair, 5:02 AM CT Fri. Rockets on Friday and Friday's weather settle after the deadline, so they are finals-only material. I verified that the TAM-OU kickoff is 20:45Z (2:45 PM CT Sat). It is therefore not the on-stage promo.

7) ECONOMICS SLIDE (all four critics). A 300-cover game night with '$5 back if the Spurs lose' carries $1,500 of tail liability. Unhedged, there is a 14% chance of losing $1,500 in one night. Hedged, the cost is a fixed ~$225 ($210 at the 0.14 ask plus spread), known before the first pour. A broker charges probability plus margin, quotes over days and has minimums. The answer to 'why lock a vault if you hedge?': the escrow is the customer's trust, and the hedge is the merchant's P&L.

8) SCOPE (all four critics). QuickNode and Switchboard are deleted from the plan and become roadmap lines only. The LLM scan gets 15 seconds on stage and falls back to templates. The program stays at 6 instructions. Spend-here and cash-out are plain SPL transfers that the merchant co-signs as fee payer, so the program doesn't change.

9) NUMBERS THAT ADD UP (past-winners #8). Every promo pays a $1 refund per receipt, and every card prints its numbers. The crank pays 10 receipts per transaction, so 20 refunds take 2 crank transactions, and the stage says '2 transactions'.

Winning patterns used: a parametric payout that is visible on stage (TX Delay Insurance, JetLagged), one hard number up front, a 'try to cheat it' segment whose attempts revert onchain, a deep sponsor integration that the sponsor could adopt, one complete path, and a recorded fallback plus a cold rerun.

research_findings.finding: Texas A&M vs Oklahoma (NCAAF-2611211700-TAM-OU-M) has startTime 2026-11-21T20:45:00Z, which is 2:45 PM CT. The ticker's '1700' and the rules text ('12:00 PM') are stale and do not match. Live book: TAM 0.26/0.29, OU 0.71/0.74. Spread and total markets are post_only with no book.

research_findings.finding: Bars hedging promos by hand on Kalshi is now a news genre. The Jeffrey (NYC) put $5,000 against a Knicks free-tab promo. Rizzo's (Chicago) put $2,000 on Mexico for a potential payout of $3,721, to cover $100 gift cards redeemable on the next visit. TallBoy (DC) covered Team USA tabs. The Blue Light (SF) did a World Cup promo and reported about 40% more business. Kalshi runs a /hedging page and launched Blanket, an AI risk-mapping tool that does not execute trades.

Rizzo's 'redeemable next visit' is the precedent for our optional 'Spend it here +25%' button, and the Blue Light's ~40% lift is the merchant's reason to run promos. The positioning line is 'self-serve and escrowed, on Gemini'.

research_findings.finding: Gemini's developer docs list Get Positions, Get Settled Positions and Get Order History for prediction markets, but the pages we fetched do not state which key roles may call them. Only the WebSocket positions@account docs explicitly accept the Auditor role.
research_findings.how_used: The Auditor-REST question stays a 30-minute test at H2. The decided fallback order is: Auditor over WebSocket positions@account, then an attestor-only second Trader key (disclosed). The re-attestations at cutoff and pre-settlement read positions (not orders), which is what actually proves the hedge was held.

Spurs vs Clippers (NBA-2611200100-LAC-SAS-M) tips off at 7 PM CT Thursday with Clippers YES at 0.13/0.14. The sandbox has 0 weather and 0 sports markets. The settled-event JSON includes volume24h, which keeps changing after resolution. quantityMinimum is 0.01.

changes_vs_current: ONE-LINER cut to one sentence plus a rivalry: 'Your drink's on us if the Spurs lose: hedged on Gemini, guaranteed onchain.' The pitch line: 'Kalshi signs up bars one at a time by phone. Hedgehog is self-serve and escrowed, on Gemini.' The problem slide shows four Kalshi bar headlines as proof of demand.

REFUND MADE USEFUL WITHOUT GIVING IT BACK TO THE MERCHANT: the USDC is pushed to the customer's browser wallet and the customer owns it. Two optional buttons: 'Spend it here' ($1 counts as $1.25 off the next visit; the customer signs, the merchant pays the fee) and 'Cash out' (to any Solana or exchange deposit address). Honest label on the receipt: devnet test dollars now, real USDC in production. No default return to the merchant.

WEATHER PAIR REFRAMED as ONE merchant's 'wrong-weather promise' (our team's coffee cart): '$1 back on iced drinks if under 74°F' and '$1 back on hot drinks if 74°F or warmer'. The cart covers whichever slow day comes. It is still certain that one side pays, and the pitch says so. It is no longer two stands with opposite promises.

HEDGE-HELD RE-ATTESTATION: attest_hedge(phase = OPEN, CUTOFF or PRESETTLE) stores the held fraction per phase. The receipt shows 'Hedge held at kickoff ✓'. New attack #5: sell 1 contract back after cutoff, and the receipt flips to 'Hedge reduced: your $1 is still in the vault'.

CANONICAL RESOLUTION HASH (ticker, instrumentSymbol and resolutionSide per contract, resolvedAt, in sorted-key JSON) replaces the raw-JSON sha256. Verify is tested against an event resolved more than 24 h earlier.

CALENDAR FIXED: the submission video uses Thursday settlements only (Spurs ~10 PM CT Thu, weather pair 5:02 AM CT Fri). Rockets Friday and Friday weather settle before finals and appear only there. The Aggies game (kickoff verified at 2:45 PM CT Sat) is dropped as the live promo. The live finals promo uses the first game that starts after our slot, with a pre-created fallback.

TRACK DECIDED: DeFi & Onchain Apps (the hedged-promise primitive: hedge-gated issuance composed with an external regulated venue; the README already covers economic design and risk assumptions). This answers 'B2B with a consumer receipt' and keeps Consumer from being a mid-pack bet.

ECONOMICS SLIDE added: 300 covers × '$5 back if the Spurs lose' = $1,500 tail. Unhedged: a 14% chance of a −$1,500 night. Hedged: a fixed ~$225. Next to it, a broker's days of quoting plus minimums, and 'escrow = customer trust, hedge = merchant P&L'.

SCOPE: QuickNode and Switchboard deleted from the build plan (roadmap only). The LLM scan gets ≤15 s on stage with a template fallback. The live order on stage is a bonus, and the recorded production fill with order ids is the primary evidence.

NUMBER HYGIENE: every receipt pays $1. The crank pays 10 receipts per transaction, so the stage line is '20 refunds in 2 transactions'. Every promo card prints cost per receipt, liability, premium and max receipts.
design.problem: Bars already run 'free tab if the team wins/loses' promos because they fill seats. The Blue Light in SF reported about 40% more business, and Mattress Mack built a brand on it. Every one of these promos is a fat-tail liability. In 2026 the fix was a news story told one bar at a time. The Jeffrey put $5K on Kalshi for the Knicks, Rizzo's put $2K on Mexico to cover $100 gift cards, TallBoy covered Team USA tabs in DC, and Mattress Mack put $516K on the Astros. Each was set up by hand, often with Kalshi's own outreach team on the phone. None of them gave customers any proof the payout would happen. The alternative is a prize-indemnity broker that quotes over days, prices at probability plus margin, and sets minimums no food truck meets. So an Austin coffee cart or a Guadalupe sports bar can't safely say 'your drink's on us if the Spurs lose' on a $6 ticket. Its customers also have no reason to believe a small shop will pay tomorrow. Gemini already lists the events these promos depend on: Austin and San Antonio daily highs, and Texas NBA and NCAA games. They settle within hours on public data. What's missing is the self-serve layer. It needs to turn one sentence into a priced promise, buy the hedge before the first sale, lock the customers' refunds where the owner can't touch them, and pay those refunds automatically as money the customer actually owns. Longer term, the same rails let small businesses replace insurance with exchange-traded cover for weather, game nights and input costs.
design.target_user: Primary: Austin owner-operators whose sales swing with weather and game nights, such as watch-party bars on Guadalupe and 6th, coffee and frozen-drink trailers, food trucks and patio bars. They already run promos, can't afford a bad night, and won't get Kalshi's phone outreach. Beachhead: sellers near UT (student-org coffee and bake sales, campus carts) whose customers are students. Honesty rule: the demo merchant is our own team's cart or watch party, labeled 'demo merchant: our team'. A real Austin business is named only if it actually takes part or gives a recorded quote. Secondary: the customer, who pays nothing extra, installs nothing, and ends up holding $1 they can spend at the shop for $1.25 or cash out.
design.how_it_works:
1) READ THE BUSINESS (≤15 s on stage). The owner types 'sports bar on Guadalupe, $6 drafts, ~150 covers on game nights'. An LLM call with a fixed tool schema maps the description onto a catalog of live Gemini series only: AUS and SAT daily highs, and Texas NBA, NCAAM and NCAAF moneylines. Template cards are the fallback. Books come from the public REST API (30-s cache, retry on 500). Start times always come from the event's startTime field, never from the ticker.

2) PRICE PROMISE CARDS. There are up to 3 cards. Each has a plain-English sentence plus Gemini's contract text verbatim, and each pays a $1 refund per receipt. Examples: 'Spurs lose tonight → $1 back' (Clippers YES, ask 0.14); 'Under 74°F at Austin-Bergstrom → $1 back on iced drinks' (strip ≤69 + 70-71 + 72-73, Σasks 0.47); '74°F or warmer → $1 back on hot drinks' (Σasks 0.65). Each card shows cost per receipt, fair value from mids, spread paid, maximum receipts the book depth supports at the limit price, the vault lock, and a scale preview (300 covers → liability and premium). Basis risk is zero by construction, because the promise's terms are the contract's terms. Fractional contracts (quantityMinimum 0.01) keep strip sizing exact.

3) LOCK, THEN HEDGE (one tap). create_promise moves L = cap × $1 into a vault PDA. It records the strip (up to 6 contract tickers), refund_units, cap, sales_close_ts (from startTime, or noon CT for a same-day high), the attestor and relayer pubkeys, and a terms hash. The agent sends a Gemini /order/batch with one limit buy per bin at ≤ ask+$0.02, sized for a 10-receipt tranche, and cancels any remainder after 30 s. The attestor reads fills (Auditor key) and calls attest_hedge(phase = OPEN, qty per bin, avg price, sha256(order ids)). Capacity = min over the bins of qty / refund_units.

4) SELL (crypto invisible). The customer pays normally. The counter screen shows a one-time QR code, and scanning it opens /r/[code]. The page creates a browser keypair (localStorage, plus a copyable backup link with the secret in the URL fragment). The merchant server calls issue_receipt and pays the fees and ATA rent. The program reverts with SalesClosed, SoldOut or Unhedged ((sold+1) × units > attested capacity). At ≤3 receipts of capacity remaining, the agent buys the next tranche within its price limit and daily budget. Otherwise the promo sells out. It never hedges more than the liability.

5) HOLD. At sales cutoff and again 30 minutes before expected resolution, the attestor reads positions@account and calls attest_hedge(phase = CUTOFF or PRESETTLE). The program stores the held fraction (in basis points) per phase. The receipt shows 'Hedge held at kickoff ✓', or 'Hedge reduced: your $1 is still in the vault'.

6) SETTLE. The worker polls the event (weather from 10:55 UTC, games from startTime + 2 h). The relayer calls attest_outcome(winning_contract_index, canonical_hash), where canonical_hash = sha256 of the sorted-key JSON {ticker, contracts:[{instrumentSymbol, resolutionSide}], resolvedAt}. The program marks YES if the winning index is in the strip. Gemini's own rule that an undeterminable result resolves NO is inherited verbatim. On YES, a permissionless refund_crank pushes $1 USDC to 10 receipts per transaction. On NO, release returns the vault to the merchant. Either way the merchant's net promo cost equals the premium paid, and on YES Gemini pays $1 per contract into the merchant's own Gemini account.

7) THE CUSTOMER'S DOLLAR. The receipt flips to '$1.00 is yours'. 'Spend it here' builds an SPL transfer of $1 to the merchant: the customer's browser key signs, the merchant co-signs as fee payer, and the counter applies $1.25 off (a merchant-set bonus that drives repeat visits). 'Cash out' sends to any pasted Solana or exchange deposit address. Neither path touches the program, and the merchant cannot claw the money back.

8) VERIFY. 'Verify with Gemini' re-fetches api.gemini.com/v1/prediction-markets/events/{ticker} in the customer's browser, builds the canonical subset, hashes it, and compares the result with the onchain value and the resolution side.

PROGRAM (Anchor hedgehog_promise, 6 instructions): create_promise, attest_hedge(phase), issue_receipt, attest_outcome, refund_crank, release. Errors: SalesClosed, SoldOut, Unhedged, LiabilityLocked, UnauthorizedAttestor, AlreadyRefunded, NotSettled.

AGENT LIMITS (README): limit orders only, at ≤ ask+2c; never hedges more than the liability; daily premium budget of $25 by default; per-promise price ceiling of 0.70 per $1 of refund; stops and closes sales on any Gemini error or empty book; holds no onchain withdrawal authority.

ECONOMICS (slide and README): a 300-cover game night with '$5 back if the Spurs lose' carries a $1,500 tail. Unhedged, there is a 14% chance of a −$1,500 night. Hedged, the cost is about $225, fixed and known before the first pour, and settles in hours. The escrow is the customer's trust, and the hedge is the merchant's P&L. Capital in v1 is a 100% lock for ≤24 h. On the roadmap, Gemini winnings refill the float through USDC-on-Solana withdrawal, and a settle-to-address request goes to Gemini.
design.why_crypto: A promo only works as advertising if customers believe it, and a small shop can't make a stranger believe it will pay tomorrow. The hand-built Kalshi bar promos give customers no proof at all. The chain does four things a POS database can't. (1) The refunds sit in a program vault before the first sale. Anyone can see the balance from the receipt, and the merchant cannot pull it out before Gemini's result is posted (LiabilityLocked). (2) The rules that make it a hedged promo rather than a gamble are code every customer can inspect: no sales after kickoff (SalesClosed), and no receipt beyond the hedge capacity reported by a disclosed attestor (Unhedged). Hedge-held status is recorded at cutoff and before settlement. (3) Anonymous walk-up customers get paid with no card, email, bank account or chargeback. The receipt PDAs are the eligibility list, and the crank pushes $1 to hundreds of people for fractions of a cent within seconds. Card refunds can't do this: interchange fees, the original-card rule, and multi-day app redemption all get in the way. (4) The $1 belongs to the customer. They can spend it back at the shop for $1.25 or cash it out, and nobody can revoke it. A gift-card table in the shop's own database can't promise that. USDC on Solana is also Gemini's own withdrawal rail, so in production the hedge winnings and the customer refunds meet on one chain. Trust stated plainly: a disclosed Hedgehog relayer, whose result anyone can check against Gemini's public API, and a disclosed Hedgehog attestor that reads the merchant's Gemini account. Neither can move vault funds to itself.
design.demo_moment:
0:00 OPEN (20 s). The opener is four headlines: The Jeffrey, Rizzo's, TallBoy and The Blue Light, all hedged by hand on Kalshi. Then: 'Kalshi signs up bars one at a time. Mattress Mack hedged his Astros promise with $516K. On Thursday night our watch party hedged "Spurs lose, your drink's on us" with $2.80 on Gemini, in 30 seconds, self-serve.'

0:20 THE PAYOUT, already settled and certain (40 s). Our coffee cart ran a wrong-weather promise on Thursday: $1 back on iced drinks if under 74°F, $1 back on hot drinks if 74°F or warmer. One side had to pay, and we say so. Gemini resolved the Austin high at 5:02 AM Friday. On screen: 20 refunds in 2 crank transactions on Explorer, a phone reading '$1.00 is yours', a tap on 'Spend it here' that shows $1.25 off at the counter, and Verify with Gemini matching the canonical hash. The Spurs result is shown as it happened. If the Spurs lost, it's more refunds. If they won, it's a vault release and the line 'the bar's whole cost was $2.80.'

1:00 LIVE FLOW (90 s). Type 'sports bar on Guadalupe, $6 drafts, game nights'. Three cards appear in under 15 s. Pick tonight's game, chosen Saturday morning as the first game that starts after our slot. One tap: the vault locks, the Gemini batch order fills a 10-receipt tranche, and order ids appear on screen. The live fill is a bonus; if it errors, we show Thursday's recorded production fill. Capacity reads 10. Two judges scan on their phones and get receipts that say 'If the Spurs lose tonight, $1 comes back to you.' Labeled: 'on the house today; in a bar it rides on your draft.'

2:30 CHEAT THE PROMISE (60 s; each attempt is a red failed transaction or a flipped badge). (1) Receipt #11 before the top-up → Unhedged. (2) A receipt after kickoff → SalesClosed. (3) The merchant pulls the vault → LiabilityLocked. (4) The merchant key posts 'NO' → UnauthorizedAttestor. (5) We sell 1 contract back on Gemini after cutoff → the receipt flips to 'Hedge reduced: your $1 is still in the vault.' Then: 'The vault is the customer's guarantee. The Gemini contract is the merchant's.'

3:30 ECONOMICS (30 s). 300 covers, $5 back if the Spurs lose: a $1,500 tail. A 14% chance of losing $1,500, or a fixed $225 before the first pour.

4:00 VISION and CLOSE (30 s). The same engine covers a restaurant's natural gas, a food truck's diesel, and heat in summer: insurance replaced by exchange cover. Then a cold rerun of create → hedge → receipt in 20 s, and the closing line: 'Every bar promo on Kalshi was hand-built. Ours is one sentence, hedged on Gemini before the first sale.'

sponsor_tech.tech: Gemini Prediction Markets API (public REST, production Trader key for /order/batch, read-only Auditor key for attestation via positions@account)
sponsor_tech.how_core: Gemini is in the money path. Every promise is priced from Gemini books (strip sums, depth caps), and every receipt is backed by real production contracts bought before sales open. Hedged and held quantity is read from the merchant's Gemini positions at OPEN, CUTOFF and PRESETTLE and gates issue_receipt onchain. The promise text is Gemini's contract text, the trigger is Gemini's resolutionSide, and the winnings are Gemini's $1-per-contract payout. Sandbox is used only for CI tests of the order and attest code, because the sandbox has no weather or sports markets.

Holds the refund vault and issues receipt PDAs. Enforces the startTime cutoff, the cap, hedge-gated issuance (Unhedged), per-phase hedge-held records, relayer-only settlement over a contract strip with a canonical resolution hash, and a permissionless refund crank of 10 receipts per transaction. Every refund and every stage attack runs against it.

Vault liability, pushed refunds, 'spend it here' transfers and cash-out are all USDC. A $1 refund unit maps 1:1 to a $1 Gemini contract. The production refill path is Gemini's API withdrawal of USDC on Solana.

sponsor_tech.tech: Fee-payer co-signing (the merchant pays fees and ATA rent)
sponsor_tech.how_core: Keeps crypto invisible. Customers never fund or install anything. Their browser key signs only when they choose to spend or cash out, and the merchant co-signs as fee payer.

design.prize_fit: PRIMARY: Gemini Prediction Markets bounty ($2.5k plus a finals slot). This is the most Gemini-native entry: real production fills on Gemini's weather and sports books, which sandbox-only competitors cannot show. Gemini's contract text is the consumer terms, resolutionSide is the payout trigger, and the pitch frames it explicitly as the self-serve, escrowed Gemini answer to Kalshi's hand-built bar hedges. MAIN TRACK: DeFi & Onchain Apps. It is a new primitive (hedge-gated, escrowed promise issuance composed with an external regulated venue), and the README covers economic design, risk assumptions and addresses. Consumer Apps is the fallback if the second project also lands in DeFi; the spend-or-cash-out loop and the crypto-invisible frontend support either. CHAIN AWARD: Best use of Solana. Custom program, the Unhedged invariant, per-phase hedge-held records, cheap pushed refunds to anonymous holders, and fee-payer UX. OFFICIAL UBC: a real settled payout, Texas stories (Mattress Mack, the Spurs), and judges holding receipts that pay out that night. Distinct from Spendthrift (agent-wallet revocable checks) and Shed (grid compute).
design.why_novel: The 2026 bar-hedge genre (Jeffrey, Rizzo's, TallBoy, Blue Light, Mattress Mack) is hand-built, Kalshi-only and gives customers no proof. Kalshi's Blanket recommends hedges but doesn't execute, hold funds or settle. Brokers quote over days and never reach a $6 ticket. Onchain weather and sports cover projects (Arbol, RainTokens, AridGuard and others) write their own risk with homemade pools. Hedgehog is a hedged-promise primitive. A customer refund (a) is written word for word against a regulated exchange contract or strip, so the promise and the hedge can't diverge; (b) can only be issued once a disclosed attestor has reported the hedge fill, with hold status re-recorded at cutoff and before settlement; and (c) is pre-funded in escrow and pushed to anonymous customers as money they own, with a public canonical check against Gemini's API. We found no project that combines self-serve promo generation from live prediction-market books with a hedge-gated issuance invariant and crypto-invisible pushed refunds.
design.build_plan:
Team: 2 humans plus Claude Code agents, in the existing Next.js repo (lib/gemini.ts, lib/solana.ts, lib/math.ts, lib/store.ts). H0 = Wed 1 PM CST. Deadline H47 (Fri 12:00 CST).

H0-4 GATE, before any Anchor code. A KYC'd production Gemini account accepts PM terms through the API, creates a Trader key and an Auditor key, places a $0.03 limit buy on a Thursday AUS bin, and reads it back. Timebox for the Auditor read: 30 min over REST, then positions@account over WebSocket, then an attestor-only Trader key (disclosed). If no production fill by H4, switch projects that hour. Budget $75. In parallel: Anchor/Solana CLI, 5 devnet wallets (merchant, attestor, relayer, crank, attacker) and Circle devnet USDC; DM 3 businesses near UT.

H4-14 PROGRAM MVP: create_promise, attest_hedge(phase), issue_receipt, attest_outcome, refund_crank, release. Tests for the happy path plus Unhedged and SalesClosed first, then the remaining errors. Deploy to devnet by H14 (Thu 3 AM CST). In parallel: strip pricing and tranche engine with unit tests on saved books, the Gemini batch order and cancel client, the attestor, and the canonical-hash relayer.

H14-20: merchant dashboard (cards → lock → hedge → capacity), counter QR, /r receipt page (browser wallet, sponsored issuance, hedge-held badge, Verify), settlement worker and crank.

H20-23 (Thu 9 AM-noon CST) RUN #1: the wrong-weather pair at our cart, ≤20 receipts per side, sales close at noon CT. If the deploy slips past H21, skip it and run #1 becomes the Spurs.

H23-30: spend-here and cash-out buttons (SPL transfer with merchant fee payer), attack panel (4 prebuilt transactions sent with skipPreflight, plus the real 1-contract sell-back), LLM scan with template fallback. RUN #2: Spurs watch party, sales close at 7 PM CT tip-off (H30), settles about 10 PM CT (H33).

H30-40: README (decision loop, limits, economics, trust, addresses, legal framing), economics slide, test Verify against an event resolved more than 24 h earlier. If run #1 was skipped, buy a Friday weather pair for finals. Fri 5:02 AM CST (H40): Thursday weather settles. Run the crank and record it.

H40-46: record the 3-minute video from Thursday settlements only, with human voiceover, then submit by Fri 11:30 CST. Friday: Rockets promo (9 PM CT tip-off) runs for finals material only.

FINALS (Sat): Saturday morning, pick the first game with startTime after our slot. Pre-create its promo, keep the recorded production fill and order ids on screen as primary evidence, bring 2 pre-funded backup phones and a full screen recording, and preload all settled links.

CUT ORDER: LLM polish (templates) → cash-out (keep spend-here) → San Antonio → Friday runs. NEVER CUT: vault, Unhedged, real Gemini fill, CUTOFF re-attest, settle plus crank, attack panel, Verify.
design.risks: 1) Production Gemini access is the single point of failure (KYC, PM terms, API trading, position reads). It is gated at H4, with a switch-project rule and no faking in sandbox. 2) Thin books: about 20-40 contracts per bin caps each promo at 20-30 receipts. Tranches plus SoldOut handle it, the card shows max receipts, and sales close on any Gemini 500. 3) Real money: about $60 of premium across all runs, disclosed. Devnet refunds against production hedges is a stated mismatch, labeled 'test dollars'. The production bridge is the Gemini USDC-on-Solana withdrawal, shown as code. 4) Settlement timing is measured (weather +6 h, games +3 h). If one is delayed, the video shows the attestation with the crank pending. 5) Trust: one operator holds the relayer and the attestor, disclosed as least privilege. The proof is the customer-side Verify. 6) Capital: a 100% lock for ≤24 h in v1. The economics slide explains escrow versus hedge. 7) Key loss: a localStorage wallet with a fragment backup link and early cash-out. 8) Optics and legal: a uniform purchase rebate (Mattress Mack and broker genre). Customers never choose outcomes or see odds, only the KYC'd merchant trades, and we say 'confirm with counsel'. Judges' receipts are labeled on-the-house samples. 9) Copycat perception (the Kalshi bar genre) is turned into the problem slide and the rivalry line. 10) Scope: the program must be deployed by H14 for the weather run, and the Spurs fallback buys 9 hours. 11) Track: if the second chosen project is also DeFi, the two entries split the judges, which is the reason for the Consumer fallback.
open_intricacies: Can an Auditor-role key read PM positions over REST, or only over WebSocket positions@account? Test in a 30-minute timebox at H2. The fallback order is decided.
Can the teammate's retail production account place PM orders through the API, including /order/batch? Untested until the H0 $0.03 order.

Which game is the finals live promo? It depends on the finals schedule and Saturday's catalog. Rule: the first game with startTime after our pitch slot. If there is none, crank an already-settled promo from team phones and use a pre-created promo for the attacks.
Track: DeFi (the default) versus Consumer depends on which two of Hedgehog, Spendthrift and Shed are chosen, so the two entries don't compete in one track.
The 'Spend it here' bonus: is a 25% bonus (the merchant's cost) the right default, or should it be configurable per merchant with a default of 0%? The current default is +25% on the demo cart.
Whether a real Austin business near UT gives a recorded quote or runs a Friday trial. Outreach is in progress, and nothing is claimed until it happens.

Whether the attack #5 sell-back uses a real Gemini sell of 1 contract (costs the spread, most convincing) or a lower attestation posted from a reduced test position. Default: a real sell of 1 contract.

critiques.best_change: Two changes do the most work: naming the Kalshi bar-hedge genre outright on the problem slide, and the line "Kalshi does this by phone, one bar at a time. Hedgehog is self-serve and escrowed, on Gemini." Before, a judge who had read about Rizzo's or The Jeffrey would quietly mark this down as a copycat. Now that news coverage is the proof of demand, and the Gemini bounty judges get a competitive reason to care. The calendar fix also matters a lot: the video uses Thursday settlements only, and the Aggies game is dropped because its startTime collides with finals. That removes a likely failure on stage.
critiques.worst_change: The "Spend it here" +25% bonus. It adds a second loyalty mechanic, a co-signed transfer flow, a counter discount UI, and another number for judges to track. It also muddies the clean story ("your $1 comes back"), and the label still reads "test dollars (devnet USDC)". A merchant-funded bonus on devnet money that a judge can't actually spend sounds like a feature for a deck. Close second: the hedge-held re-attestation (CUTOFF and PRESETTLE phases) plus attack #5. It is clever, but it sells a Gemini contract with real money on stage, and it adds a sixth beat to a 5-minute pitch that is already overloaded.
objections: Originality is now openly borrowed. The core idea, a bar hedging a sports promo on a prediction market, is a 2026 news genre, and Blanket does the AI mapping. What's new is narrower: hedge-gated escrowed issuance plus pushed refunds. If that isn't the thing judges remember, this reads as 'Kalshi bar promo, but on Gemini'.

The pitch is too crowded for 5 minutes: four headlines, Mattress Mack, a weather pair, Spurs, a live flow, two judge phones, five attacks, an economics slide, a vision and a cold rerun. Judges will remember one moment at most. Pick it: the payout, or Unhedged reverting.

The devnet/production mismatch is still the soft spot. The hedges are real money and the refunds are play money. 'Money the customer owns' falls apart when Q&A asks 'can I spend this $1 anywhere real?' and the honest answer is no.

The weather pair is certain to pay because the team ran both sides at its own cart. A sharp judge will call it staged: 'you sold a promise that always pays and called it a demo.' It's honest, but it's not organic. With no real Austin merchant on record, the 'local businesses' claim is still aspirational.

The economics slide invites an obvious Q&A attack. A $225 hedge against a $210 expected loss is insurance at a premium, plus a 100% capital lock on top. 'Why both escrow AND hedge? You're paying twice for one risk' needs a crisp 10-second answer. The current line ('escrow = customer trust, hedge = merchant P&L') is close but abstract.

The track choice is shaky. DeFi judges want composable primitives and risk modeling. A trusted off-chain attestor reading a CEX account is not composability in their eyes. Consumer fits the crypto-invisible receipt better, but the judges' phones then show test dollars.
Single point of failure: production Gemini API trading with KYC, PM terms and an untested Auditor role. A fair H4 kill switch, but if it trips, two days of iteration are wasted.

The trust story is still 'trust Hedgehog's attestor and relayer', with both keys held by one operator. The Verify button checks the outcome, not the hedge, and the hedge status is attested from a private account.
critiques.what_would_make_it_win: Cut it to a single memorable moment and sharpen the one-line identity to "Your drink's on us if the Spurs lose, and the chain won't let the bar sell it unless the bet's already placed." Make the Unhedged revert the hero, shown live: receipt #11 fails until the agent buys the next Gemini tranche, and then it succeeds. No other entry can show that, and it is the actual invention. Then cut it down: 3 attacks, not 5 (Unhedged, LiabilityLocked, UnauthorizedAttestor). Drop the +25% bonus, or make it a one-line roadmap item. Merge economics into one 10-second line ("$210 expected, $225 fixed, known before the first pour"). Get ONE real Austin business near UT to run even a 10-receipt promo, or give a recorded 15-second quote; that alone moves Impact more than any mechanism. Finally, for Q&A, prepare a one-sentence answer to "why escrow and hedge both?": "The hedge pays the bar tomorrow morning on Gemini, but the escrow pays the customer tonight, guaranteed even if the bar vanishes." Do those and this is a credible Gemini 1st plus a Solana-track contender. As written, it's top-3 in its track but at risk of being remembered as 'the busy Kalshi-bar one'.

critiques.best_change: The calendar fix and the hedge-held re-attestation. The current best's live beat relied on the Aggies game, which actually kicks off at 2:45 PM CT Saturday, during finals. That would have broken on stage, and this version catches it and builds the video only from Thursday settlements. The CUTOFF and PRESETTLE attest_hedge phases, plus a real 1-contract sell-back on Gemini that flips the receipt to 'Hedge reduced: your $1 is still in the vault', answer the sponsor objection that a hedge can be bought and then dumped. They also show the split between escrow (protects the customer) and hedge (protects the merchant) more clearly than any slide could. The canonical-subset hash (leaving out volume24h) fixes a real bug where Verify would have failed after resolution.
critiques.worst_change: Moving to the DeFi & Onchain Apps track and adding 'Spend it here +25%'. A DeFi judge expects onchain composability (CCTP, protocols, onchain liquidity). Here the 'primitive' composes with an offchain centralized exchange through a trusted attestor, and the vault is 100% pre-funded. That invites the question: 'If the vault already covers every customer, what does the onchain Unhedged gate protect?' The honest answer is that it protects the merchant from its own agent. That is a spending-control story, not a DeFi primitive. The +25% spend-back button adds scope, recycles money to the merchant (close to the store-credit idea rejected earlier), and runs on devnet 'test dollars' while the counter gives a real-world discount. Judges will see that as theater. Leading the one-liner with 'Kalshi signs up bars' also tells Innovation judges the market already exists, though Gemini judges will like the rivalry framing.
objections: Trust hole judges will hit in Q&A: with a 100% USDC lock, the customer is already fully protected without any hedge, so Unhedged/hedge-held enforce nothing for the customer. They are guardrails on the merchant's own P&L, reported by an attestor that Hedgehog itself runs. Say this plainly ('the gate protects the merchant from its own agent; the vault protects the customer'), or a sharp judge will call the gate decorative.

The whole bounty case depends on one unverified gate: whether a KYC'd retail Gemini account can trade prediction markets through the API (/order/batch) at all. If that fails at H4, there is no sandbox fallback with weather or sports markets. The switch-project rule is correct, but it means the expected value is really about 0.6-0.7 times this score.

Devnet refunds are paid against production hedges. The money the customer 'owns' is test USDC, while the Gemini winnings land in the merchant's Gemini account on a different rail. The story that the customer's dollar is real and can't be revoked is only true on the roadmap. Keep the label honest and don't let 'Spend it here' imply real value.

The weather pair amounts to buying the whole strip: about $1.12 of premium per pair of $1 payouts, with one side certain to pay. A judge will call it 'a rebate with extra spread'. It works as a demo device to guarantee a settled payout, but don't present it as a hedge.

Thin books (20-40 contracts per bin, a ≤69 bin with no bid, Gemini 500s) cap each promo at about 20-30 receipts. The 300-cover economics slide describes a size the live book can't fill today, and judges may check the depth.

Scope is still heavy for 47 hours and 2 humans: a 6-instruction Anchor program with phases, a strip hedge engine, an attestor with an uncertain Auditor read path, a relayer, a crank, a browser wallet, fee-payer UX, an attack panel, Verify, an LLM scan, and spend/cash-out. The program must deploy by H14 (3 AM Thursday) or run #1 is lost.

Legal and optics: a CFTC-regulated account trading on sports outcomes to fund consumer rebates, on stage in front of a regulated exchange's PM. 'Confirm with counsel' is thin. Have one prepared sentence on why this is a uniform purchase rebate and not a sweepstakes or wager.
critiques.what_would_make_it_win: Pick Consumer Apps unless the second project forces DeFi. If you stay in DeFi, rewrite the primitive claim as an 'agent-hedged liability with onchain spending limits'. Then make the gate do real work by cutting the vault from 100% pre-funded to a partial reserve: lock only the merchant's worst-case loss beyond the attested hedge (for example, a 30% reserve plus attested hedge ≥ 100%), so the Unhedged rule is what makes partial funding safe. That turns the attestation into the thing that frees up capital, which is the honest DeFi primitive, and it answers 'why both?'. Drop the +25% spend-back from the critical path and keep Cash out. Pass the H0 production-API gate with an order id on screen. In the 3-minute video, show one real Thursday payout (20 refunds in 2 transactions, plus a Verify match) and the 5-attack panel, in under 90 seconds combined. Close on the Mattress Mack line, which already lands.

critiques.best_change: Fixing the calendar and the trust surface together. Thursday-only settlements for the video, start times read from the startTime field (the TAM-OU ticker says 17:00 but kickoff is 2:45 PM CT Sat), and a canonical resolution hash with volume24h excluded. These remove the two ways the earlier version could fail outright: a video promising refunds that settle after the deadline, and a Verify button that would mismatch on stage. Turning the Kalshi bar stories into a problem slide also helps. It applies the "real users / proof of demand" rule (Colosseum: "evidence that a team is solving a real problem") and answers "isn't this just Kalshi's /hedging page?" before a Gemini judge asks it. Making the $1 a customer-owned dollar instead of store credit also answers the "database would do" objection (ETHDenver's "why blockchain?").
critiques.worst_change: The economics slide contradicts our own risk section. "300 covers × $5 back if the Spurs lose = $1,500 tail, hedged for a fixed $225" needs about 1,500 Clippers YES contracts. Risk #2 says the books hold roughly 20-40 contracts per bin and cap a promo at 20-30 receipts. A sharp DeFi judge will multiply it out in Q&A, and the slide that was supposed to prove impact shows the product can't scale on Gemini's current liquidity. Close behind it is scope creep that adds nothing the customer can see: hedge-held phase attestations (CUTOFF/PRESETTLE), a real 1-contract sell-back attack, and spend-here at +25% with a counter redemption flow. Together they add 3 new moving parts to a build that already depends on a KYC'd production Gemini account nobody has tested. Judge research says "one complete path beats four half-built paths", and the attack segment has grown from 4 failed transactions to 5 beats in 60 seconds.
objections: The 'one sentence' one-liner is four sentences, and the 0:00 opener now leads with four headlines plus Mattress Mack before saying what the product is. Kurbaitaev: 'teams that lost ground opened with context'. State 'Hedgehog: promos for Austin bars, hedged on Gemini, refunds guaranteed onchain' in the first 5 seconds, then show the headlines.

Liquidity contradicts the economics. A $1,500 hedge doesn't exist on a book 20-40 contracts deep. Show the economics at the depth Gemini actually has (e.g. a 30-receipt promo for about $4.20 in premium), and present the scale story as what happens when liquidity grows, not as today's product.

Hedge-held re-attestation is cosmetic for the customer. The vault already covers them whether or not the hedge is held, and the program does nothing on reduced hedge. A judge will ask 'so what happens if the hedge drops?' and the answer is 'a badge changes'. Either gate something on it (block release or new tranches) or cut it to roadmap.

Attack #5, the real sell-back, depends on a bid existing. Several weather bins show no bid ('-/0.03', '-/0.10', '-/0.01'). It works only on the Spurs/Clippers contract, so state that, or drop the attack.

'Spend it here' turns devnet test dollars into $1.25 of real product. That honesty mismatch invites the question 'so the customer's dollar isn't real?' Keep the button, but have the demo show a balance and a transfer, not a counter discount.

'Kalshi signs up bars one at a time over the phone' is an attack on a competitor, and the sources only say Kalshi has a /hedging page and outreach. If Kalshi's flow is self-serve, a judge who knows it will mark us down for overstating (Rule 11). Soften it to 'hand-built, unescrowed, no customer proof'.

Switching from Consumer to DeFi goes against the evidence in our own notes. Prediction-market consumer apps win Consumer tracks (Pregame, Trepa, Capitola, Fora), while DeFi winners are protocol primitives (Urani, Yumi). This build is a merchant dashboard plus a crypto-invisible receipt page, which is a Consumer-shaped artifact. DeFi judges will ask about the economics, which is where the liquidity hole is.

The single point of failure is still untested after 4 iterations: retail production Gemini PM API trading, /order/batch, and Auditor position reads. Everything ranks below that H0 $0.03 order. The pitch also still requires a 100% USDC lock plus the premium, so the merchant pays for the same cover twice. Expect 'why not just one of them?'

The weather pair is staged to be certain. Buying both strips costs Σasks of about 1.12 per paired $1. Fine as a demo, but say plainly that the merchant sells these to different customers, otherwise it looks like a rigged payout.
critiques.what_would_make_it_win: Cut back to what judges will actually see. Open in one sentence. Show one settled payout with Explorer proof and Verify with Gemini (already the strongest beat, matching the TX Delay Insurance and JetLagged parametric-payout pattern). Run one live hedge plus judge receipts, then 4 red cheat transactions. Base the economics on the depth Gemini actually has (a 30-receipt promo, premium of about $4, 'the bar's whole cost was $2.80') and present liquidity growth as the opportunity Gemini owns, not a gap. Move the CUTOFF/PRESETTLE phases and the sell-back attack to roadmap unless they gate an instruction. Get one real Austin merchant quote or Friday trial; that is the single biggest remaining jump on Impact (Colosseum: talk to users). Run the H0 production-order gate tonight, before anything else, and keep Consumer as the track unless the second project forces DeFi. Do this and it's a credible Gemini 1st-place contender at about 8.5.

critiques.best_change: The calendar fix. I checked the live data: Spurs-Clippers startTime is 2026-11-20T01:00Z (7 PM CT Thu) with LAC at 0.13/0.14, and the Thursday AUS strip still reads 74-75 at 0.48/0.53 and 72-73 at 0.27/0.32. Using only Thursday settlements in the video, and dropping the Aggies game because its startTime collides with Saturday finals, removes the biggest demo-timing risk of v3. The rule 'read startTime, never the ticker' is the kind of detail that saves a live demo. The canonical-subset hash comes second: it removes the volume24h drift that would have made Verify fail on stage.
critiques.worst_change: The 'wrong-weather promise' reframing. With $1 back on iced drinks if under 74°F and $1 back on hot drinks if 74°F or warmer, the customer picks an outcome by picking a drink. That breaks the README's own legal line, 'customers never choose outcomes'. The merchant also buys the full partition (0.47 + 0.65 ≈ 1.12 per pair), which is a guaranteed loss of the spread. A Gemini judge will see a staged certain payout, not a hedge. In second place, 'Spend it here +25%' plus 'Cash out' adds a co-signed transfer flow and a merchant POS discount step on top of devnet test dollars. A bar honoring $1.25 off for a devnet token is incoherent, and it costs H23-30 build time that the hedge-held and attack work needs.
objections: Single point of failure, still ungated: nobody has shown that a retail production Gemini account can place prediction-market orders through the API (including /order/batch) and read positions with an Auditor key. KYC, accepting PM terms and state eligibility can take days, not 4 hours. Switching projects at H4 throws away 4 of 47 hours. This needs to be tested tonight, before any other work.

The economics slide contradicts the risk section. The slide prices 1,500 Clippers contracts at 0.14, while the risks section says books hold about 20-40 contracts per bin. One real 300-cover night can't be filled on Gemini today, so a sharp judge will ask 'who fills this?' Present it as 'today: 20-30 receipts per promo; liquidity grows with merchant flow / Gemini market-making', or the slide undermines credibility.

Devnet refunds against real production hedges: the customer's dollar is fake while the merchant's hedge is real. 'Money back' is the emotional core, and the receipt says 'test dollars'. Judges will accept it but discount the Consumer/Impact score. The asymmetry should be stated once, plainly, not hidden in a label.

Human bandwidth: 1-2 people must run a physical coffee cart Thursday 9 AM-noon (H20-23) and a Spurs watch party Thursday 7 PM, with about 20 real customers each, while finishing the program, the attestor, the WebSocket position reader, the crank and the UI. In practice the receipts will come from teammates' phones. Say so ('20 receipts issued by team and friends') or the 'real customers' framing invites an honesty question.

Program deploy by H14 (Thu 3 AM CST) with 6 instructions, phase-aware attest_hedge, strip handling and a 10-per-tx crank using remaining_accounts is achievable with agents, but tight. Pushing to receipt ATAs also needs the customer ATA created at issuance (the merchant pays about 0.002 SOL rent per receipt). Budget devnet SOL from the manual faucet early, because airdrop is closed.

positions@account over WebSocket is an event stream, not necessarily a snapshot. The CUTOFF and PRESETTLE re-attestations may need the REST Get Positions with a Trader key anyway. Expect the 'Auditor' least-privilege story to degrade to a second Trader key.
Gemini production returned 500s on Nov 18. The live finals order should be framed as a bonus from the first second. Never put a cold fill on the critical path of the 5-minute pitch.

Too much is going on: 5 attacks, 3 attestation phases, spend/cash-out, LLM scan, economics, vision, cold rerun, all in 5 minutes. The demo script at 4:30+ will overrun. Cut to 3 attacks (Unhedged, LiabilityLocked, UnauthorizedAttestor) plus the hedge-reduced flip.

Trust: one operator holds both the attestor and the relayer, so 'program rule' still reduces to 'Hedgehog's signature'. That's fine if disclosed, but Best use of Solana judges may note that the novel invariant (Unhedged) depends entirely on an offchain oracle.
critiques.what_would_make_it_win: 1) Tonight, before writing any Anchor code: place a $0.03 production PM order through the API and read positions back. That one fact decides the project. 2) Replace the two-sided weather pair with ONE one-sided promise that every customer gets regardless of what they order. Example: 'Under 74°F tomorrow → $1 back on today's drink' (strip asks ≈ 0.47, a near coin-flip, so roughly 50% odds of a visible payout). Keep the Spurs promise (14%) as the second shot, and have Friday weather ready for finals. Honest odds, no customer choosing an outcome, no guaranteed spread loss. 3) Fix the economics slide to match real Gemini depth: 'today one promo = 20-30 receipts; here's the order book; Hedgehog merchant flow is new taker demand for Gemini's weather/sports books.' That last line is the sentence Gemini wants to hear. 4) Cut spend-here/cash-out to a single 'Cash out' button, or none: the receipt flipping to '$1.00 is yours' plus a Solscan link is enough. Spend those hours on the attack panel and a rock-solid recorded fill with order IDs and the positions read. 5) Keep the pitch to one Mattress Mack line, one settled payout, one live fill (bonus), three red transactions and one Verify match. The current script is about 30% too long for 5 minutes.
